prompt: You're writing the README for `browser/brave_rewards/`. It already states the directory's purpose. Which section should come next to orient a new developer?
choices: A full list of every file in the directory, sorted alphabetically
A changelog of recent PRs that touched the directory
Key files, each with a one-line description of its role
A copy of the class comments from each header file
explain: An orienting README names the key files and their roles (e.g. `rewards_service_impl.cc` is the main implementation, `rewards_service_factory.cc` the profile-keyed factory) rather than dumping everything.

prompt: A draft README for the Rewards browser integration has a purpose statement and a key-files list. A reviewer says it's still missing something a newcomer needs. What is most likely missing?
choices: A Usage section showing how to obtain the service
A full API reference duplicated from the service headers
A history of why the service was originally designed this way
Build instructions copied from the main brave-core README
explain: A good README covers purpose, key files, how to use the main APIs, and who maintains it. Start with the simplest use case, such as how to obtain the service.

prompt:
A PR adds this to a Brave component README:

```markdown
## How to Add a Feature Flag

1. Create a feature in features.h...
2. Register in about_flags.cc...
3. Add a histogram entry in enums.xml...
```

The steps are copied from Chromium's docs. What should the reviewer say?
choices: Fine, as long as a comment notes which Chromium revision it was copied from
Fine; having the steps inline saves readers a click to another site
Move the copied steps into a separate `FEATURE_FLAGS.md` file instead
Link to the upstream guide instead; a copy will go stale
explain: Don't duplicate documentation: copies inevitably drift out of sync. Link to the canonical source instead. (Entries in `docs/best-practices/` are the exception and must be self-contained.)

prompt: In a general project README, which version of a "How to Add a Feature Flag" section follows Brave's documentation guidance?
choices: A full step-by-step copy of the Chromium guide, with Brave notes added inline
A link to the Chromium guide plus the Brave-specific `about_flags.cc` step
Just a bare link to the Chromium guide, with no other text at all
A note telling readers to search the Chromium docs for "feature flag"
explain: Link to the canonical source with context: point to Chromium's feature flag guide and add only the Brave-specific note, which is to also register in `brave/browser/about_flags.cc`.
